speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger first started, and has there been any recent injury or insect bite? Also, is the pain constant, or does it come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Okay, that sounds like a traumatic injury. Can you tell me if the finger is bent at an unusual angle or if it feels unstable when you move it? Also, is there any visible deformity or bruising you've noticed since it happened?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to flex your distal joint and the finger resting in an extended position are classic signs of a tendon rupture. I need to confirm if you can still feel sensation in the fingertip and if there is any visible laceration or bruising at the tip. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Hand.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger. Hand Examination: Right ring finger is extended with visible swelling and tenderness at the distal interphalangeal joint; patient is unable to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint while attempting to make a fist. Neurovascular assessment shows normal capillary refill and no sensory deficits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the mechanism of injury and your inability to flex the distal joint, I strongly suspect an injury to the flexor tendon. To be certain, I need to rule out a bone avulsion, so please REQUEST TEST: MRI Right Hand.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI of the Right Hand: Preliminary findings expected to show details regarding the integrity of tendons. (Note: Final detailed results pending radiologist review).

speaker: Doctor
text: While we wait for the final MRI read, I need to know if you noticed any skin nick or cut at the fingertip during the injury, or if the skin remained intact. Can you also describe exactly how much force was required to pull your finger straight when it happened?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the skin remained intact and the X-ray ruled out a fracture, the clinical picture of your finger resting in extension with an inability to flex the distal joint strongly suggests an avulsion fracture or a rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon, commonly known as "Jersey Finger." I have enough clinical evidence to confirm this injury pattern. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Tendon Avulsion)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
